neet_che_u12_t06_1.working: Sc3+ has a d0 configuration, so no d-d transition is possible and the complex is colourless. Ti3+ (d1), Ni2+ (d8) and Cu2+ (d9) are all coloured.

neet_che_u12_t06_2.working: [Fe(CN)6]4-: d6 low spin, 0 unpaired. [Fe(CN)6]3-: d5 low spin, 1 unpaired. [CoF6]3-: d6 high spin, 4 unpaired. [MnF6]4-: Mn2+ d5 high spin, 5 unpaired, giving 5.92 BM, the highest.

neet_che_u12_t06_3.working: E = hc/λ = (6.6e-34 × 3e8)/(600e-9) = 3.3e-19 J per ion. Multiplying by NA gives 3.3e-19 × 6e23 = 1.98e5 J/mol = 198 kJ/mol.

neet_che_u12_t06_4.working: A is true: MnO4- is intensely coloured. R is true as the general d-d explanation for most complexes. However, Mn(VII) is d0, so its colour arises from ligand-to-metal charge transfer, not d-d transitions. R therefore does not explain A.

neet_che_u12_t06_5.working: I: Co3+ is d6 and NH3 makes it low spin (t2g6), so it is diamagnetic with 0 BM; I is incorrect. II: en is a stronger-field ligand than H2O, so Δo increases and the complex absorbs shorter wavelengths; II is incorrect.
